page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running on a KVM hypervisor. It features 24 vCPUs spanning 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server incorporates 48.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-focused hardware profiles. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES-NI hardware encryption, and FMA.

The instance relies entirely on remote block storage, providing zero local NVMe or SSD storage capacity. Network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline. In benchmark evaluations, single-core processing scores lower relative to wider cloud server datasets, as seen in stress-ng single-core (1313.3) and gzip single-threaded compression tests. However, parallel workloads perform within the middle tier, supported by a stress-ng multi-core score of 21007.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8967.0. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 108.94 GB/sec for reads and 47.99 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput measures 20.09 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 15.86 GB/sec.

From a resource-density perspective, the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation minimizes memory overhead for compute-bound tasks, offering cost efficiency for workloads that do not demand large memory capacities per thread. The absence of included ephemeral storage requires pairing with external network volumes. The ecs.c6.6xlarge is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation, web serving, microservices, and compute-heavy ETL workloads.
